def reverse_string(s: str) -> str:
    return s[::-1]
explanation: Python's slice notation s[::-1] creates a new reversed string in linear O(N) time with minimal overhead.

Initialize largest with the first element nums[0], then iterate through the remaining elements updating largest whenever a greater number is found. This correctly handles lists containing entirely negative numbers in O(N) time and O(1) space.
Filter characters with c.isalnum() and convert to lowercase with c.lower(). Comparing the resulting list to its reverse verifies palindromicity in O(N) time.

Use a seen set to record elements encountered and a duplicates set to collect elements seen more than once. Sorting the unique duplicates yields the desired ascending output in O(N log K) time, where K is the number of distinct duplicates.

Iterate through the array maintaining a hash map of value -> index. For each number, check if target - num exists in the map. If found, return [lookup[complement], current_index]. This runs in optimal O(N) time and O(N) space.
